newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux cuts more stringent than expected.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux cuts more stringent than expected.

text.p: The world's largest appliance maker, Sweden's Electrolux AB, unveiled a hard-hitting two year restructuring programme on Thursday under the beady eye of tough, new managing director, Michael Treschow.

After just two months at the helm, Treschow announced Electrolux would close about 25 of 150 plants and cut 12,000 staff from a workforce of 105,000 in a 2.5 billion crown ($321.6 million) programme which will be charged against second quarter earnings.
The share price -- usually sluggish -- soared a massive 50 crowns to 512 by 1400 GMT as markets welcomed the news.

Analyst Andrew Griffin from UBS said the market had expected Treschow, head of industrial engineer Atlas Copco until April this year, to wield the axe against Electrolux's falling profits and tough conditions in Europe.
"But this is much stronger than people anticipated," Griffin told Reuters.
"This is much more radical than anything Electrolux has done before."

Analysts say Electrolux shares have been weighed down for several years by shrinking markets and by a perception that former chief executive Leif Johansson -- now head of car maker Volvo -- was not tackling the roots of the company's problems.
Under Treschow, known as a cost cutter with a focus on shareholder value, analysts expected a similar clarity of vision as he brought to Atlas Copco.
"(Electrolux) needed to do something about its profitabilty and that was what Mr Treschow was brought in to do," said a Stockholm based broker.
"There was a positive reaction in the market place (to the announcement) but it was not a total surprise."
Analyst Angelica Hanson from Matteus brokerage welcomed the restructuring programme.
"It has come earlier than we thought but it shows there was a lot of dead meat which comes as no real surprise," Hanson said. "It's good that the costs will be taken out directly."
Electrolux said the restructuring costs levied in the second quarter would be partly offset by a capital gain of 600 million crowns from the sale of Husqvarna Sewing Machines.
Griffin said Treschow's plan gave the market some hope that he would also split off other parts of the group.
"The share price is discounting the idea of creating shareholder value by splitting off non-core assets which the previous management seemed unwilling to do," he said.
Electrolux said in a statement that the restructure was designed to boost profit margins.
Electrolux has set a long-term financial target to reach an operating margin of 6.5-7.0 percent by the year 2000.
In 1996, Electrolux posted a 19 percent drop in profit after financial items of 3.25 billion crowns, blaming weak European markets.
In the first quarter of 1997, Electrolux's profit dipped 14 percent against a year ago, again attributed to the difficult market situation in Europe.
"The white goods market has been weak for nine successive quarter but in the first quarter (of 1997) there were signs it could be about to turn, including in Sweden," said Hanson.
"It is good to see concrete steps and not just talk."
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 7.774 Swedish Crowns)
